A.explanation: A basketball is larger than the 0.12 m football, but the Moon is smaller than the Earth so its model must be smaller.

B.explanation: A cherry has radius of order 0.01 m, which is about three times too small for the calculated $0.032 \text{ m}$ model Moon.

C.explanation: A golf ball has radius of about $0.021 \text{ m}$, which is noticeably smaller than the $0.032 \text{ m}$ required for the scale Moon.

D.explanation: A tennis ball has radius of about $0.033 \text{ m}$, which matches the calculated scale radius of about $0.032 \text{ m}$ for the Moon.

hints: Compare the two real radii $6.4 \times 10^6 \text{ m}$ for Earth and $1.7 \times 10^6 \text{ m}$ for the Moon with the model Earth radius of $0.12 \text{ m}$.
A scale model keeps the same ratio, so the model Moon radius equals $0.12 \text{ m}$ multiplied by the real ratio $1.7/6.4$.
Work out that product in $\text{m}$, convert to $\text{cm}$, and ask which listed object has a radius near $3 \text{ cm}$ rather than much larger or much smaller.
walkthrough: Identify the scale rule: $\text{model radius} = \text{real radius} \times \text{scale factor}$, where the scale factor is fixed by the Earth model.
Find the real size ratio: $r_{Moon}/r_{Earth} = (1.7 \times 10^6 \text{ m})/(6.4 \times 10^6 \text{ m}) \approx 0.266$, so the Moon is about one quarter the radius of the Earth.
Apply the same ratio to the model: $r_{model Moon} = 0.12 \text{ m} \times 0.266 \approx 0.032 \text{ m}$.
Check size: $0.032 \text{ m} = 3.2 \text{ cm}$ radius, so diameter about $6.4 \text{ cm}$. This is much smaller than a football but much larger than a cherry.
A tennis ball with radius about $3.3 \text{ cm}$ is the closest match. This is option D.
